title: RadiusOnlyGeneralizedSmoothConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained convex minimization of f:E→ℝ, with an attained minimum and some minimizer xstar satisfying ‖x0−xstar‖≤R.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query x returns precisely ∇f(x), for every history and seed. No function values or noisy gradient information are supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable everywhere and ‖D(∇f)(x)‖≤L0+L1‖∇f(x)‖. L0,L1,R,ε are strictly positive.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space. Public information consists of E,L0,L1,x0; R and ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor and enter only the external oracle budget. No initial objective-gap bound is supplied.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RadiusOnlyGeneralizedSmoothConvex.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, execute

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap inequality holds almost surely under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the fixed supplied gradient-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Convex exact-gradient optimization with gradient-dependent curvature, arbitrary Hilbert-space geometry, and an algorithm that is not given the radius or target accuracy is a meaningful variant of the classical smooth convex benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Generalized Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a convex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth, with L0>0 and L1>0, and has an everywhere differentiable gradient. A given starting point x0∈E lies within distance R>0 of a global minimizer x⋆. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, and ∥⋅∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The algorithm receives only E, L0, L1, and x0; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Generalized smoothness). The function f and its gradient ∇f:E→E are Fréchet differentiable everywhere. The Hessian ∇2f(x):E→E satisfies ∥∇2f(x)∥op≤L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥,x∈E.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. Here x⋆ is fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness; all global minimizers have the same objective value.

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import LongTails.Template

namespace LongTails.Setups.RadiusOnlyGeneralizedSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 < q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ k seed x, HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k (0, x) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed, Differentiable ℝ (fun x => oracle.answer k (0, x) seed)) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y => oracle.answer k (0, y) seed) x‖ ≤
      q.L0 + q.L1 * ‖oracle.answer k (0, x) seed‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.RadiusOnlyGeneralizedSmoothConvex
